subject.title: [Bug]: --to flag ignored when using --agent with custom channel, all sessions map to main

question: Should explicit `openclaw agent --agent --channel --to` use raw recipient-derived session keys, or require bounded or opaque keys plus upgrade handling before the fix lands?
rationale: The bug is valid, but the fix changes persisted session identity and may expose recipient identifiers, so automation should not choose the privacy and compatibility contract for maintainers.

options.title: Refresh With Bounded/Opaque Keys
options.body: Refresh or replace the open PR on current main, preserve explicit selector precedence, and use a bounded or maintainer-approved opaque recipient key contract with upgrade handling.

options.title: Accept Raw Recipient Keys
options.body: Land raw channel/recipient-derived keys only after the PR body and tests make that persisted identifier contract explicit and accepted.

options.title: Pause For Design
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose a different compatibility or privacy design before implementation continues.

recommendation.title: Refresh With Bounded/Opaque Keys
recommendation.body: Refresh or replace the open PR on current main, preserve explicit selector precedence, and use a bounded or maintainer-approved opaque recipient key contract with upgrade handling.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the open closing PR and have recent merged history in the same resolver/test boundary.
